caveats: AC-WIRE-3 satisfied; missing_contract PARTIAL on adapter constructor (VQ-S1-019) accepted by user — EventSignerNdkAdapter does not validate that the signer arg is truthy. In practice prevented by (1) TypeScript declaring `signer: EventSigner` (non-nullable), (2) `if (signer)` guard at the only call site in src/marmot/client.tsx:158, (3) MarmotProvider mount gate in app/page.tsx:424. If the adapter's call surface ever widens beyond MarmotProvider, add `if (!signer) throw new Error('EventSignerNdkAdapter: signer is required')` to the constructor.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: One non-obvious friction point: the architecture.md examples and spec comments refer to NDKAuthPolicies.signIn() but the actual export from @nostr-dev-kit/ndk is NDKRelayAuthPolicies (with a NDKRelayAuthPolicies.signIn method). The spec's phantom name would have compiled only if there happened to be a re-export alias, which there is not. Discovering this required reading the export list in index.d.ts. A second friction was the TypeScript structural mismatch between NDK's NostrEvent.kind (number | undefined) and applesauce-core's EventTemplate.kind (number), requiring an explicit cast in the sign() method. Neither issue is a spec deficiency — they are just cross-library shape differences that only surface at compile time.
retrospective.surprised_by: The NDKSigner interface also requires a toPayload(): string method that does not appear in the architecture.md listing. TypeScript's implements check caught this at first compile. The adapter adds a minimal JSON serialization to satisfy it.
